s: When did the Vaikom Satyagraha take place?
x: The Vaikom temple-road satyagraha was in 1924-25, led by T.K. Madhavan, K. Kelappan and K.P. Kesava Menon; Gandhi visited Vaikom in March 1925.

s: In Andhra, what was the Desasevikalu?
x: Desasevikalu was a women's wing; Durgabai met Gandhi at Kakinada in 1921 and Andhra women donated jewellery to the Tilak Fund.

s: Where did Durgabai meet Gandhi in 1921 and raise Rs 5,000?
x: Durgabai met Gandhi at Kakinada in 1921 and raised Rs 5,000.

s: Where did Kolla Tayaramma run Harijan schools and hostels?
x: Kolla Tayaramma worked at Tenali; Alladi Annapurna Devi ran Harijan schools at Nellore.

s: On which date did Gandhi speak at Mogalrajpuram, Vijayawada, during his Harijan tour?
x: Gandhi spoke at Mogalrajpuram, Vijayawada on 16 December 1933 during the Harijan tour.

s: What was the main purpose of Gandhi's tour of Andhra in 1933?
o: collect funds and campaign against untouchability
set up the Wardha Scheme schools
x: He toured Andhra on the Harijan tour to collect funds and campaign against untouchability.

s: In which year did Gandhi make his khadi tour of Andhra, during which he visited Bezawada and Vetapalem?
x: Gandhi toured Andhra for khadi in April 1929; his Harijan tour of Andhra came later, in 1933.

s: At Vetapalem in 1929, Gandhi laid the foundation stone of the building of which library?
x: During the 1929 khadi tour Gandhi laid the foundation stone of the Saraswata Niketanam library building at Vetapalem.

s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched with regard to the Gandhian sequence of firsts?
x: Kheda is associated with Gandhi’s first non-cooperation in this sequence. Champaran was the first Satyagraha in India, while Ahmedabad was associated with his first fast.

s: In which year did the Champaran Satyagraha take place in Bihar?
x: Champaran was in 1917; Kheda and the Ahmedabad Mill Strike followed in 1918.

s: Against what was the Champaran Satyagraha mainly directed?
o: Forced indigo cultivation and illegal exactions by European planters
x: European planters compelled peasants to grow indigo and, when indigo became unprofitable, demanded illegal dues and enhanced rents; forest tax was not the issue.

s: During whose viceroyalty did the Champaran, Ahmedabad and Kheda struggles take place?
x: All three struggles occurred during the viceroyalty of Lord Chelmsford, who served from 1916 to 1921.

s: Why is the period 1917–1919 considered significant in Gandhi's political career?
o: resulted in the adoption of Complete Independence as the Congress objective
marked the beginning of his political work in South Africa
established Gandhi as a national leader and Satyagraha as a method of struggle
marked the launch of the Quit India Movement
x: The Champaran, Ahmedabad and related struggles between 1917 and 1919 established Gandhi as a national leader and Satyagraha as an important method of anti-colonial struggle.

s: Which movement demanded the immediate end of British rule?
x: The Quit India Movement demanded the immediate end of British rule; Non-Cooperation was non-violent non-cooperation.

s: Where was the 'Do or Die' call of the Quit India Movement given in 1942?
x: The Quit India Movement began with the 'Do or Die' call at Bombay in 1942.

s: Which of the following movements came earliest?
x: The Home Rule Movement began in 1916, before Non-Cooperation (1920), Civil Disobedience (1930) and Quit India (1942).

s: What was the aim of the Home Rule Movement of 1916?
x: The Home Rule Movement sought self-government; the immediate end of British rule was the demand of Quit India.

s: Which of the following took place first?
x: Champaran (1917) came first, followed by the Ahmedabad Mill Strike (Feb-Mar 1918), Kheda (1918) and the Rowlatt Satyagraha (April 1919).

s:
Arrange the following in chronological order:
1. Kheda Satyagraha
2. Jallianwala Bagh massacre
3. Champaran Satyagraha
4. Non-Cooperation Movement
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
x: Champaran was in 1917, Kheda in 1918, Jallianwala Bagh in April 1919 and the Non-Cooperation Movement in 1920-22.

s: Who among the following led the Home Rule Movement of 1916?
o: Lajpat Rai and Bipin Chandra Pal
x: The Home Rule Movement of 1916, for self-government, was led by Tilak and Annie Besant.

s: In which region did the Moplah Revolt of 1921 take place?
x: The Moplah Revolt (1921) was a rising of the Mappila Muslims of Malabar (Kerala) against the British and Hindu landlords.

s: At which session of the Indian National Congress was the Non-Cooperation programme first adopted in 1920?
x: The Non-Cooperation programme was adopted at the special Calcutta session of the Congress in 1920.

s: Which were the main centres of the Home Rule Movement of 1916?
x: Annie Besant's league worked from Madras and Tilak's from Poona; both sought self-government.

s: Which one of the following correctly describes Gandhi’s method during the Champaran Satyagraha?
o: He began an armed resistance against the European planters.
He accepted the order to leave the district and confined his work to petitions.
He called upon peasants to stop cultivating all food crops.
He defied the order to leave and, with his lawyers, recorded peasants’ complaints in the villages.
x: Gandhi defied the official order to leave Champaran and toured villages with his lawyers to record complaints against forced indigo cultivation. This compelled the government to order an inquiry.

s: Which of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched in the context of Champaran?
o: Mahadev Desai — Leader of the European planters
x: Mahadev Desai was Gandhi’s secretary and pledged himself to the Champaran work in 1917. He was not a leader of the European planters.

s: What was the occupation of Rajkumar Shukla, who persuaded Mahatma Gandhi to visit Champaran?
o: Lawyer of the Bihar High Court
x: Rajkumar Shukla was a local indigo cultivator and agriculturist of Champaran who persuaded Gandhi to investigate the peasants’ condition. Rajendra Prasad was an associate, not the inviter.

s: On which date did Gandhi reach Champaran?
x: Gandhi reached Champaran on 10 April 1917 with Brajkishore Prasad, Rajendra Prasad and others.

s: Who is the author of 'Mahatma Gandhi and Bihar, Some Reminiscences'?
x: Dr. Rajendra Prasad, a Bihar lawyer who joined Gandhi at Champaran, wrote this book.

s: Which of the following books was written by Dr. Rajendra Prasad?
o: Mahatma Gandhi and Bihar, Some Reminiscences
x: Rajendra Prasad wrote 'Mahatma Gandhi and Bihar, Some Reminiscences'; India Wins Freedom is by Azad, The Discovery of India by Nehru, Gandhi and Anarchy by Sankaran Nair.

s: Which event is regarded as the precursor to the Champaran indigo movement?
x: The Bengal Indigo Revolt of 1859 preceded and served as an important precursor to the later indigo-related mobilisation in Champaran.

s: Which of the following statements regarding Champaran is incorrect?
o: Plantation owners increased taxes on peasants.
Plantation owners imposed other illegal exactions on peasants.
The issue was connected with indigo exploitation.
Peasants were relieved because plantation owners reduced all taxes voluntarily.
x: Option D is incorrect: the Champaran planters raised taxes and imposed illegal levies; they did not reduce them. The issue arose from forced indigo cultivation.

s: What did 'tawan' mean in Champaran?
o: Lump-sum compensation demanded when indigo lost its value
x: Tawan was lump-sum compensation extracted when indigo became less valuable; sharahbeshi was enhanced rent.

s: What did 'Sharahbeshi' mean in Champaran?
x: Sharahbeshi was enhanced rent; tawan was lump-sum compensation and tinkathia the 3/20th indigo obligation.

s: Why had indigo become unprofitable for the European planters of Champaran by the early 20th century?
o: The British banned the export of indigo
German synthetic dyes replaced natural indigo in the world market
The Champaran Agrarian Act fixed low prices
x: German synthetic dyes made indigo unprofitable; planters then raised rents and imposed illegal dues on tenants.

s: In the Ahmedabad Mill Strike, what were the workers' demand and the mill owners' offer, respectively?
o: 20 per cent wage increase and 35 per cent increase
50 per cent wage increase and 20 per cent increase
35 per cent wage increase and 50 per cent increase
50 per cent wage increase and complete withdrawal of wages
x: The workers demanded a 50 per cent wage increase because of wartime inflation, while the mill owners offered only 20 per cent.

s: Which of the following statements is incorrect?
o: The Ahmedabad Mill Strike took place in 1918.
Workers received a 35% bonus after the result of the strike.
The dispute involved plague bonus and wages.
x: Option C is incorrect: the 1918 Ahmedabad Mill Strike lasted 21 days, not 35. It concerned the plague bonus and wages, and the workers won a 35 per cent increase.

s: Who founded the Ahmedabad Textile Labour Association, also known as Majoor Mahajan Sangh, in 1920?
o: Ambalal Sarabhai with Vallabhbhai Patel's guidance
J.B. Kripalani with Anugrah Narayan Sinha's guidance
x: The Ahmedabad Textile Labour Association (Majoor Mahajan Sangh) was founded by Gandhi with Anusuya Sarabhai on 25 February 1920; it worked through arbitration and non-violence.

s: What wage rise did the tribunal award the workers in the Ahmedabad Mill Strike (1918)?
x: The workers had demanded 50%; Gandhi advised 35% and the tribunal awarded 35%.

s: Who led the mill owners in the Ahmedabad Mill Strike (1918)?
x: Ambalal Sarabhai led the mill owners; his sister Anusuya Sarabhai stood with the workers.

s: How long did the Ahmedabad Mill Strike of 1918 last?
x: The strike lasted 21 days, not 35; 35% was the wage rise awarded.

s: The withdrawal of which allowance by the mill owners led to the Ahmedabad Mill Strike of 1918?
x: The Ahmedabad mill owners withdrew the plague bonus, and the workers demanded a 50% wage rise instead.

s: Who among the following first took up the cause of the Ahmedabad mill workers and appealed to Gandhi in 1918?
x: The workers approached Anusuya Sarabhai, who appealed to Gandhi; her brother Ambalal Sarabhai led the mill owners.

s: What did the Champaran Agrarian Act of 1918 abolish?
x: Based on the Enquiry Committee's recommendations, the Act abolished Tinkathia and secured a 25 per cent refund of illegal exactions.

s: Who chaired the Champaran Agrarian Enquiry Committee (1917), on which Gandhi represented the ryots?
x: F.G. Sly chaired the committee, appointed by the Bihar and Orissa government.

s: By whose agreement was the Champaran Agrarian Committee of 1917 appointed?
o: The Viceroy and the Secretary of State
x: The Bihar and Orissa government appointed the Champaran Agrarian Committee by agreement with Gandhiji, who sat on it for the ryots.

s: What share of the illegal charges was refunded to the peasants under the Champaran settlement?
x: The Champaran Agrarian Act, 1918 abolished Tinkathia and refunded 25% of the illegal charges.

s:
Consider the following statements about the Champaran Agrarian Act, 1918:
1. It abolished the Tinkathia system.
2. It refunded 50 per cent of the illegal dues collected by planters.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: The Act abolished Tinkathia but the refund was 25%, not 50%.

s: The Kheda Satyagraha (1918) was Gandhi's first experiment in which of the following?
x: Kheda was the first non-cooperation; Champaran the first civil disobedience and Ahmedabad the first hunger strike.

s: What was the immediate agrarian cause of the Kheda Satyagraha?
o: Demand for a 50 per cent increase in industrial wages
Crop failure due to drought or famine and refusal of revenue remission
x: The Kheda peasants suffered crop failure caused by drought or famine and sought remission or suspension of land revenue, which the government initially refused.

s: Who provided field leadership to the Kheda Satyagraha of 1918?
x: Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel gave field leadership as Kheda peasants refused to pay land revenue despite threats of confiscation.

s: In the Kheda campaign of 1918, which of the following combinations is correct?
o: Gandhi — spiritual head; Patel, Mohanlal Pandya and Narahari Parikh — mobilisation
Patel — spiritual head; Gandhi, Rajendra Prasad and Nehru — mobilisation
Nehru — spiritual head; Patel and Subhas Bose — mobilisation
Gandhi — spiritual head; Sarojini Naidu and Annie Besant — mobilisation
x: Gandhi acted as the spiritual head, while Patel, Mohanlal Pandya and Narahari Parikh led the mobilisation among the peasants.

s: On which condition did the government settle the Kheda Satyagraha in 1918?
o: Land revenue was abolished in Kheda district
Revenue was to be collected only from those able to pay

s:
Consider the following statements about the end of the Kheda Satyagraha (1918):

2. Confiscated property was to be returned.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: The government agreed to suspend revenue for poor peasants and return confiscated property, so Gandhi called off the struggle.

s: With which satyagraha did the Gandhi-Patel alliance begin?
x: In Kheda (1918) Vallabhbhai Patel was the field commander under Gandhi; this began the Gandhi-Patel alliance.

s: Kheda district, the scene of the satyagraha of 1918, is in which present state?
x: Kheda is in Gujarat; Champaran is in Bihar.

s: Where did Gandhi form the Satyagraha Sabha against the Rowlatt Act on 24 February 1919?
x: The Satyagraha Sabha was organised at Bombay on 24 February 1919; members took an oath to disobey the Act.

s: Under the Rowlatt Act, for how long could political suspects be detained without trial?
x: The Act allowed detention without trial for up to two years, with trials by three High Court judges and no appeal.

s: On which occasion had the crowd gathered at Jallianwala Bagh on 13 April 1919?
x: The crowd gathered on Baisakhi, 13 April 1919, amid the Rowlatt Satyagraha protests and arrests of local leaders.

s: Which of the following statements regarding the firing at Jallianwala Bagh is NOT correct?
o: The firing continued for about ten minutes and involved 1,650 rounds.
The crowd had assembled in a walled garden.
The only exit was blocked by Dyer's troops.
The crowd was given a clear warning and sufficient time to disperse before firing began.
x: Statement D is NOT correct: Dyer gave no warning and no time to disperse. He blocked the only exit of the walled garden and fired without warning for about ten minutes, using 1,650 rounds, so A, B and C are correct.

s: According to official figures, what were the casualties in the Jallianwala Bagh firing?
x: The official figures recorded 379 deaths and 1,100 injuries, although the Indian National Congress estimated a higher death toll.

s: After the Hunter Committee condemned General Dyer's conduct, which body backed him?
x: The Hunter Committee, appointed after the massacre, condemned Dyer, but the House of Lords supported him.

s: Who resigned from the Viceroy's Executive Council in protest against the Jallianwala Bagh massacre?
x: C. Sankaran Nair resigned from the Viceroy's Executive Council; Tagore renounced his Knighthood and Gandhi returned the Kaiser-i-Hind medal.

s: Which Amritsar leader was arrested in April 1919, before the Jallianwala Bagh massacre?
x: Dr Saifuddin Kitchlew was the Amritsar leader arrested on 9 April 1919, before the massacre.

s: Who was the Lieutenant Governor of Punjab at the time of the Jallianwala Bagh massacre?
x: Michael O'Dwyer was Lieutenant Governor of Punjab; Brigadier-General Reginald Dyer ordered the firing.

s: At Jallianwala Bagh, Dyer's troops fired about how many rounds in some 10 minutes?
x: About 1,650 rounds were fired in around 10 minutes; 379 dead and 1,100 injured were the official figures.

s: Which one of the following was NOT a journal associated with Mahatma Gandhi?
x: Mathrubhumi was not associated with Gandhi. Young India, Navajivan and Harijan were among his journals.

s: Who was Gandhi's political mentor?
x: Gopal Krishna Gokhale was Gandhi's political mentor; Tolstoy, Ruskin and Thoreau were his intellectual influences.

x: Phoenix Settlement was set up in 1904 near Durban; Tolstoy Farm in 1910 near Johannesburg.

s: As which day is Gandhi's return to India on 9 January 1915 now observed?
x: 9 January, the day Gandhi returned in 1915, is observed as Pravasi Bharatiya Divas.

s: Where was Gandhi's Satyagraha Ashram, established in 1915?
x: The Satyagraha Ashram at Kochrab was set up in 1915, followed by Sabarmati (1917) and Sevagram (1936).

s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Gandhi's first major public speech in India – February 1916
x: Gandhi's BHU speech was in February 1916; he returned in January 1915, led Champaran in 1917 and the Ahmedabad Mill Strike in 1918.

s: Near which city in South Africa was Gandhi's Tolstoy Farm (1910)?
x: Tolstoy Farm (1910) was near Johannesburg; the Phoenix Settlement (1904) was near Durban.

s: Where did Gandhi deliver his first major public speech in India in February 1916?
x: His first major public speech in India was at BHU in February 1916.

s: Who first called Gandhi the 'Father of the Nation'?
x: Subhas Chandra Bose gave the title 'Father of the Nation'; Tagore gave 'Mahatma'.

s: What is the title of Gandhi's autobiography?
o: The Story of My Experiments with Truth
x: His autobiography is The Story of My Experiments with Truth; Hind Swaraj is another of his writings and Unto This Last is Ruskin's.

x: The Phoenix Settlement was founded in 1904; Gandhi reached South Africa in 1893 and set up Tolstoy Farm in 1910.

s: Where was Gandhi tried for sedition in March 1922 ('The Great Trial')?
x: Gandhi was tried at Ahmedabad on 18 March 1922.

s: Who was the judge who sentenced Gandhi in the sedition trial of 1922?
x: Judge Broomfield sentenced Gandhi to six years, following Tilak's case.

s: The sedition charge against Gandhi in 1922 rested on three articles in which journal?
x: The charge was based on three Young India articles, including 'Tampering with Loyalty' and 'Shaking the Manes'.

x: Gandhi was arrested on 10 March 1922 and Banker got one year; statement 2 is wrong as Gandhi pleaded guilty.
